payload.name: Preserve explicit qualifiers during extraction
payload.description: When extracting a memory from a message that contains explicit descriptive adjectives or evaluative terms (e.g., awesome, amazing, terrible), preserve those exact qualifiers in the memory content instead of replacing them with paraphrases.
content: During candidate extraction, copy explicit descriptive adjectives and evaluative phrases from the source message into the memory content whenever they describe a durable attribute of the subject or relationship.
Do not silently replace a stated quality (e.g., 'awesome') with a broader paraphrase (e.g., 'supportive') that drops the original specific description.

solves: Construction extraction failed when a concrete evaluative qualifier ('awesome') was replaced by a broader inferred paraphrase, leaving the stored memory unable to answer a direct question about the stated quality. The reusable failure is losing explicit descriptive adjectives during candidate extraction. Future sessions should preserve original evaluative terms in memory content so any later question about that stated quality can be answered from the stored evidence.
